sheet-1.description: The north-east corner of Norwood as drawn in April 1926, at 100 feet to an inch. The main block of the sheet lies south of Rockland Avenue, which crosses the page near its middle and is marked as the line between Harrington Township to the north and the Borough of Norwood to the south. Summit, High and Livingston run down the sheet to Hudson Avenue, and at the right edge two streets both lettered Railroad Avenue flank the Northern Railroad of New Jersey (Erie). The blocks are laid out in narrow numbered house lots, most of them still vacant; the buildings drawn are scattered frame dwellings with a few auto garages and sheds, and one garage and repair shop on Tappan Road. North of Rockland Avenue a strip at the left of the sheet continues the map into Harrington Township, showing Tappan Road and the head of Summit with large lots and a handful of dwellings. The upper right of the page is taken up by the atlas index of specials, a key map of the whole borough at about 1000 feet to an inch with the four sheet areas coloured, the title cartouche (population 1400, prevailing winds west), a note on water facilities and the fire department, and a small locator map of New Jersey; that area is left out of the georeferenced mask. Hudson Avenue runs across the lower part of the sheet, with the beginning of blocks that continue on sheet 2 below it, and a short street lettered Jay appears at the lower right between Livingston and the railroad.
notes: Summit, High and Livingston are printed without a suffix; today they are Summit Street, High Street and Livingston Street.
The street west of the Erie line lettered Railroad Avenue is West Railroad Avenue today.
The railroad between the two Railroad Avenues is lettered N.R.R. of N.J. (Erie), the Northern Railroad of New Jersey, now abandoned through Norwood.
Masked out: index of specials, key map at about 1000 feet to an inch, title cartouche, water and fire notes, and the New Jersey locator map.

map, 100 ft. North-east Norwood: Rockland Av (township line), Summit, High, Livingston, Hudson Av, two Railroad Avs by the Erie; Tappan Rd strip north of Rockland. Upper right holds the index, key map (about 1000 ft/in), title and notes: masked out. One part.

sheet-2.description: The business centre of Norwood in April 1926, at 100 feet to an inch. Central Avenue crosses the upper part of the sheet from Summit at the left to the Northern Railroad of New Jersey (Erie) on the right, and South Avenue crosses the lower part. North of Central Avenue are Winter, Clinton Place, High, Livingston, Jay, Oak and Chestnut, with dwellings, a saw mill and a coal storage shed beside the railroad. On Central Avenue between High and Livingston stand the Borough Hall and fire house with several stores, and the passenger depot of the Erie line is on the east side of the tracks at Central Avenue. South of Central Avenue the blocks between Summit, High and Livingston are drawn with long narrow lots and a scattering of frame dwellings; the public school, of brick, stands on Summit near South Avenue. Livingston bends south-east across the sheet towards the railroad, and two streets lettered Railroad Avenue run beside the tracks, one on each side. Below South Avenue are Clinton Street and Seymour, laid out in lots with few buildings. The right margin carries no-exposure notes along the edge of the mapped area, and the scale bar and copyright line sit in the lower left.
notes: Central Avenue is Broadway today.
Winter is Norwood Place today; Clinton Place is Clinton Avenue.
The street lettered Railroad Avenue west of the Erie line is West Railroad Avenue today.
Seymour has no matching named street in OpenStreetMap.
Clinton Street and High at South Avenue carry residuals of about 6 m in opposite directions; the drawn spacing between them is about 10 m wider than the modern one.

map, 100 ft. Centre: Central Av (now Broadway), Winter (now Norwood Place), Clinton Pl (Clinton Avenue), Summit, High, Livingston, Jay, Oak, Chestnut, South Av, Clinton St, Seymour, Railroad Avs by the Erie. Pilot sheet. One part.

sheet-3.description: The western part of central Norwood in April 1926, at 100 feet to an inch, from the West Shore Railroad at the left edge to Summit at the right. Central Avenue crosses the upper part of the sheet, passing a stone bridge over a creek near Blauvelt; north of it are large open lots and, between Tappan Road and Summit, Winter with the Norwood Presbyterian Church. Tappan Road runs straight down the middle of the sheet. To its left lies a newer subdivision of narrow numbered lots on curving and diagonal streets: Depot Place, Hill, Hillside Avenue, Valley Road, Demarest Avenue, Blanche Avenue and Mills Avenue, with very few buildings and several poultry houses. Vervallen runs west from Tappan Road. East of Tappan Road the blocks towards Summit are divided into large lots with dwellings and the Immaculate Conception Roman Catholic Church. The lower edge is marked Sec. 3 and the left and bottom margins carry no-exposure notes. A short stretch of South Street meets Summit at the right edge.
notes: Central Avenue is Broadway today; Vervallen is Vervalen Street.
Valley Road is Carpenter Avenue today; Demarest Avenue is Glenn Avenue; the lower part of Hillside Avenue, south of Vervallen, is Grissom Street.
The lower Depot Place is roughly Valley Place today; its junctions with Mills and Blanche carry residuals of about 7 m and were left out.
South Street at the right edge is South Avenue today (lettered South Avenue on sheet 2).
Hill and the upper Depot Place have no matching streets in OpenStreetMap.

map, 100 ft. West centre: Central Av (Broadway) from the West Shore RR to Summit, Tappan Rd, Vervallen, Hillside Av (lower part now Grissom St), Valley Rd (Carpenter Av), Demarest Av (Glenn Av), Blanche Av, Mills Av, Depot Pl, Hill, Blauvelt, Winter. One part.

sheet-4-1.description: The north-west part of Norwood in April 1926, at 100 feet to an inch, drawn turned so that north points to the upper left. The part runs from Rivervale Avenue at the top to Blanche Avenue and Brook at the bottom, and from the boundary with Harrington Park on the left to Railroad Avenue and the West Shore Railroad on the right. It is a large subdivision of narrow numbered lots crossed by the 120 ft wide Main and by Demarest, Everett, Trout, Carter, Cross, Burlington and Adams, with 2nd, 3rd and 4th Streets and Birch Place in the upper left, where Rivervale Avenue bends. Most lots are vacant; the buildings are frame dwellings with a few stores and garages. Near Central Avenue and the railroad are Holdrum and Broad, the West Shore passenger depot, coal storage and a hay and grain storage building, and a creek crosses the lower part under concrete and stone bridges. Harrington Avenue, Belden Place and Norwood Place lie in the lower part. A row of paper blocks north of Rivervale Avenue, on Elm, Ash, Summit, Oak, Park and Brook, is marked no exposure. The dash-dot borough line between Norwood and Harrington Park runs inside the left edge beside a heavy line that separates the inset at the lower left (part 3).
notes: Main and the north-west end of Rivervale Avenue (from Main to 2nd Street) are Broadway today; Railroad Avenue north of Central Avenue is Frasco Avenue.
Harrington Avenue and Blanche Avenue together are Blanch Avenue today.

Birch Place and Belden Place junctions did not agree with the fit (9 to 23 m) and were left out (3rd Street / Birch Place and Belden Place / Blanch Avenue excluded; 4th Street / Birch Place rejected). Broad Street was left out at both ends (Blanch Avenue 7 m, Broadway 5 m from the fit, the latter on a narrow edge pair).
Cross and Main have no streets of those names today; Elm, Ash, Summit, Oak, Park and Brook north of Rivervale Avenue were paper streets with no matching junctions.
Detected with ink_below_paper 80 for this part; with the default threshold only 7 to 8 junctions were found.

map, 100 ft. Three parts: 1 main map turned (north up-left): Rivervale Av to Blanche Av west of the West Shore RR (Main and NW Rivervale now Broadway, Railroad Av now Frasco Av, Harrington Av + Blanche Av now Blanch Av); 2 strip at right: Blanche Av from Tappan Rd past Summit (own north arrow, helmert); 3 inset lower left: Blanche Av at Livingston (anchored on one junction).

sheet-4-2.description: An inset strip at the right of sheet 4 showing Blanche Avenue from Tappan Road, at the top edge, south past Summit, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with its own north arrow pointing up and to the right. It lies east of the West Shore Railroad and is not continuous with the main map of the sheet beside it. Summit crosses diagonally near the top, where the Church of the Holy Communion (Episcopal) stands with its rectory; the rest of the strip is lined with large lots and frame dwellings on both sides of Blanche Avenue, numbered 340 to 360 on the east side. Clinton Street is lettered at the right edge. The lower part is marked Sec. 5 and the right margin carries a no-exposure note. The strip continues south in the inset at the lower left of the sheet (part 3).
notes: Blanche Avenue is Blanch Avenue today.
Placed from two junctions only (Blanch Avenue at Tappan Road and at Summit Street): helmert transformation, low confidence.

sheet-4-3.description: A small inset at the lower left of sheet 4 showing Blanche Avenue south of the strip in part 2, down to Livingston, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with its own north arrow pointing up and to the right. It shows large lots on the east side of Blanche Avenue, numbered 329 to 339, with a few frame dwellings and one store or outbuilding, and Livingston leaving the avenue towards the north-east at the bottom. The area is marked Sec. 4, Sec. 5 and Sec. 6, and the left and bottom margins carry no-exposure notes. A heavy line separates it from the main map of the sheet.
notes: Blanche Avenue is Blanch Avenue today; Livingston is Livingston Street.
Anchored on the single junction of Blanch Avenue and Livingston Street with the atlas scale (4.0 px/ft) assumed: low confidence.
